info.title: DevInsight telemetry ingest
info.description:
The only way telemetry from the Godot game Ascent enters the database.

**Retry contract.** The client's offline queue decides what to do from the status code alone: **2xx** — done, clear it from the queue (including partially rejected batches and duplicates); **4xx** — the server will judge this payload the same way every time, so drop it rather than retry forever; **5xx** — the server or database failed, keep it and retry. Every response below is chosen to keep that contract true.

**Exactly once.** With per-session `seq` numbers (logger 0.7.0+), retrying a batch that was already stored is harmless: it is skipped and reported in `duplicates`.

This document is checked against the code in `lib/openapi.test.mjs`: every limit, enum and status code here is probed against the real validator and handler.

post.summary: Record a batch of samples and events for one play session
post.description: Validates each sample and event independently: a malformed row is dropped and reported, and the rest of the batch is stored. The session, samples and events are written in a single database transaction.

backlog.summary: Two queued samples and a death, from a 0.7.0 client

200.description: Stored. Also returned when some rows were rejected or were duplicates — check `rejected` and `duplicates`. Partial acceptance is deliberate: failing a whole batch over one bad row would make it a poison pill the client retries forever.

400.description: The request as a whole is unusable: not JSON, no valid session, samples not an array, or a malformed sent_at. Do not retry.

401.description: Missing or wrong X-Ingest-Token, when the server requires one. Do not retry.

413.description: Too large: more than 256 KB, or more than 200 samples or events. Do not retry as-is; split the batch.

500.description: The server is not configured (missing database settings).

502.description: The database write failed. Nothing from this request was stored (it is one transaction). Retry.

IngestToken.name: X-Ingest-Token
IngestToken.description: Keeps casual traffic out. It ships inside the game binary, so it is not a secret and does not authorise anything beyond appending validated telemetry. Optional: a server without one configured accepts requests without it.

sent_at.description: The client's clock at the moment it sent this request (logger 0.7.0+). The server never trusts the client's clock directly: it dates each sample as (server time) − (sent_at − created_at), so a player whose clock is hours wrong still gets correct timestamps.

samples.description: May be empty (e.g. the session-ended message).

id.description: One play session, generated by the client at launch.

build_version.description: The game build. Applied to every sample in the request: a sample never names its own build.

ended.description: Sent once, on a clean shutdown. A session that simply stops reporting is recorded as abandoned — a crash cannot announce itself.

Sample.description: One performance reading, normally covering 5 seconds of play. Unknown properties are ignored.

seq.description: Per-session sequence number, 0, 1, 2, ... (logger 0.7.0+). (session, seq) is stored at most once: a re-sent sample is skipped and counted in `duplicates`. Gaps are reported as `samples_lost`. Omit for older clients.

created_at.description: When the sample was taken, by the client's clock. Corrected by `sent_at` (see the request). Without `sent_at` it is taken as-is; without either, the server's arrival time is used. After correction it must be no more than 5 minutes in the future and no more than 30 days old.

fps_rate.description: Frames per second over the interval.

frame_time_p95_ms.description: 95th-percentile frame time over every frame in the interval, ms.

frame_time_max_ms.description: Worst single frame in the interval, ms.

frames_sampled.description: How many frames the timings were measured over.

platform_count.description: Gameplay context: live platforms (rounded to an integer).

entity_count.description: Gameplay context: live nodes (rounded to an integer).

Event.description: Something that happened, as opposed to a periodic reading.

seq.description: Per-session event number, counted separately from samples. Same exactly-once rule.

event_type.description: A closed vocabulary: an unknown type is rejected rather than stored where no query looks.

created_at.description: When it happened, by the client's clock; corrected by `sent_at` like samples.

detail.description: Free-form context, e.g. {"cause": "lava"}. Must serialise to under 1000 characters.

accepted.description: Samples that passed validation (stored now, or already stored — see duplicates).

duplicates.description: Accepted samples whose (session, seq) was already stored by an earlier attempt. Not an error: a retry after a lost response.

rejected.description: Rows dropped by validation. The rest of the batch is still stored.

rejections.description: Present only when something was rejected; the first ten.

index.description: Position in the request's samples or events array.

clock_offset_ms.description: Server time minus client time, measured from sent_at. Already applied to the stored timestamps; reported so a badly-set clock is visible.
